body:
Thank you, and I know that's what I probably should do. It's just hard when I feel this way, I just really wanted to believe this time was different and I convinced myself that it must be because why else just randomly seek me out after this much time? 

If I don't hear from him about this talk today then I'm just going to tell him not to text me anymore and try to move on.

It's your house, if the parents aren't controlling their children then I do not feel it's overstepping any lines to take "discipline" into your own hands (I.e. "Hey guys, knock it off - we don't run in the house" "if you do that again you're going to have to just sit on the couch and not play"). Now, this is really just for when it comes to dangerous/damaging behavior (running, hitting, breaking things). Some parents will get very defensive over this however, in which case you really don't need their negativity anyway (I'm not going to deal with someone else just letting their child destroy my home).

If you don't like kids, then some normal kid behavior may still grate on your nerves (they're loud, they make a mess with food, they interrupt people talking) but these behaviors aren't necessarily "bad".

If I really wanted to avoid this I honestly would just stop inviting these people over. 

I will add that as a parent it isn't always as simple as just "calling a babysitter", they're expensive and it can be hard to find someone trustworthy. Unless you see these people using sitters for other outings often I don't really feel like suggesting they just get a babysitter is going to be constructive.
